thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Jumps 150 Points as Tesla, Oil, Dollar Jump - Barron's

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Jumps 150 Points as Tesla, Oil, Dollar Jump - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends Updated May 7, 2018 1:22 p.m. ET Oil has broken above $70 . The dollar is on a tear . Tesla (TSLA) jumped as Elon Musk threatened to turn himself into Willy Wonka .
Illustration: Bloomberg News Oh, and stocks have started the week even more bullish than they look.
Let’s start with the overall picture. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped nearly 200 points and the broader S&P 500 was up 0.6%. But the so-called internals looked even stronger. The number of stocks rising on the NYSE and NASDAQ is double the number falling, and so is the volume. The S&P 500 has edged above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. These might matter simply because lots of people think they do. On the other hand, all stock market forecasts have a roughly 50% chance of being right.
Warren Buffett told CNBC that “ this is not one of those times ” when stocks are in a bubble, although he also admitted he’s finding it hard to find bargains himself.
Oil prices continued their recent surge, rising 78 cents to $70.50, their highest level since late 2014. Helping matters is the threat of sanctions against Iran, a major global producer. Barron’s weekend pick ExxonMobil (XOM) rose 2.7%.
Dollar bears are taking it in the shorts - again.
The dollar index broke above its 200-day moving average, rising another 0.2%. Danske Bank points out that speculative traders were heavily net short of the dollar. Last week they slashed their negative bets aggressively. But Danske’s reading of the market data leads it to conclude that there is plenty of room to go.
The dollar has been slowly firming in the almost two months since President Trump tapped Larry “King Dollar” Kudlow as his chief economic adviser. Kudlow believes in a strong dollar , he doesn’t think that hurts exports, and he has the ear of the president. Shorts, be warned.
Meanwhile, two of our most colorful tycoons engaged in the kind of brawl that livens up the financial news business. Buffett at his weekend shareholders’ meeting, aka the Woodstock of Capitalism, warned Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk, aka the next James Bond Villain, not to try to take on his See’s Candies brand.
Musk, whose Twitter feed would make any investor nervous, retaliated by threatening to become Willy Wonka and launch a candy business. He is, he warned, “super super serious” about it. But he may be kidding about that. Who knows?
It didn’t scare Tesla investors. Tesla rose nearly 4%. Perhaps they like the idea that Musk might embrace a simple, cash-generative business.
Meanwhile, Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) revealed it had loaded up on Apple (AAPL) during the first quarter. The Cult of Cupertino returned the favor, rising another 3% to yet another new, record high.
S&P 500 : +0.5% to 2676.81
Dow 30 : +152.16 points, or 0.6%, to 24,414.67
Nasdaq : +0.8% to 7270.43
Vix : +0.6% to 14.86
10-year Treasury Yield : +0.01 percentage point to 2.96%
Midday Movers Dentsply Sirona (XRAY) is down 6.7% to $46.65 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The medical supply company earned 45 cents a share on revenue of $956.1 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of 42 cents on revenue of $942.2 million. However, for the full year it expects to earn between $2.55 and $265 a share, down from $2.70 to $2.80 a share in its previous guidance, and below the $2.70 per-share consensus estimate.
International Flavors and Fragrances (IFF) is down 6.5% to $132.85. Although it reported earnings of $1.69 a share on revenue of $930.93 million in the first-quarter , above the $1.60 per share and $911.6 million analysts expected, guidance was slightly below expectations, as it expects to earn between $6.21 and $6.33 a share on revenue of $3.60 billion to $3.67, compared with the $6.28 per share and $3.64 billion consensus. It also announced the acquisition of Frutarom in a $7.1 billion cash-and-stock deal.
Illustration: Getty Images Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT) is up 2.2% to $91.70, after Needham and H.C. Wainwright both lifted their price targets on the stock, to $109 and $96, respectively.
Sysco (SYY) is up 3.7% to $64.61 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The food service firm earned 67 cents a share on revenue of $14.35 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 63 cents on revenue of $14.32 billion.
Walmart (WMT) is down 2.3% to $85.51 as investors worry about its FlipKart deal . — Teresa Rivas
